lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is Tuesday's Telluride Town Council meeting, where the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code goes to its third and final reading — pass it and the Land Use Code changes, reshaping what property owners can do with landscaping and trees under historic review standards. Ridgway's council is also busy Wednesday with a public hearing on the Hyde Subdivision replatting and a joint work session on its draft Housing Action Plan. Meanwhile, the Mushroom Festival rolls into town mid-week and San Miguel County's Planning Commission takes up subdivision mechanics and an energy code update Thursday.

notable.stake: Third reading vote could permanently change landscaping and historic review rules.
Public hearing on Hyde Subdivision replatting plus housing plan review open for comment.
Energy code update and subdivision standards could reshape county building and land-division rules.
